misconceptions.description: Collecting screenshots or files with no caption explaining what they show or which skill they demonstrate
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes an image or link into the portfolio with no label
misconceptions.feedback: Each evidence item needs a caption: what it is, which skill it shows, and what you decided or revised.

misconceptions.description: Believing a longer portfolio with many items is automatically stronger evidence
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds many low-relevance items to look thorough
misconceptions.feedback: Choose a few items that each clearly map to a learning target. Quantity does not show competence; relevant evidence does.

misconceptions.description: Showing only the polished final product with no before, revision, or decision trail
misconceptions.trigger: portfolio item has a final version but no record of what changed or why
misconceptions.feedback: Include a short before/after or decision note so a reviewer can see the reasoning, not only the finished file.

misconceptions.description: Claiming a skill in a reflection without linking to an artifact that demonstrates it
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'I improved my privacy practices' with no evidence attached
misconceptions.feedback: Tie every skill claim to a specific artifact a reviewer can open, such as your privacy checklist or revised resume bullet.
